title: Microsoft Defender for Identity: unified identity timeline on the Identity page
summary: Hold: the access guidance omits permission and scoping qualifications that affect what administrators can configure and what analysts can see. The custom-role route skips permission selection, and the page incorrectly implies that cross-workload timelines did not already exist. The roadmap facts and the documented timeline columns are supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: Anyone who can open the Identity page sees the combined cross-source activity and Conditional Access policy details.
claims.quote: If you assigned read-only permissions for a single data source, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, the assigned users can't read alerts in the other services, such as Microsoft Defender for Office 365 or Microsoft Defender for Identity.
claims.fix: Replace 'Anyone who can open the Identity page sees that cross-source activity in one place' with 'The timeline consolidates activity from its source tables in one place.' Replace 'That reveals policy design to every analyst with access' with 'These event details reveal policy design.' Do not equate permission to open the page with permission to read every source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access is governed through Microsoft Defender unified RBAC without a tenant-model qualification.
claims.quote: Starting March 2, 2025, new Microsoft Defender for Identity tenants can only configure permissions through Microsoft Defender XDR Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Tenants with roles assigned or exported before this date will retain their current configuration.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-for-identity/role-groups.
